author: hoeschec
text:
USD-CHF:

The pole and FL have yet to be engulfed (to the downside). At this point, it looks like an engulf has just occurred to the north. I am awaiting a RT to the origin of the EG so I can get in the trade without having a high R:R. The better the retrace the less my risk is....

Waiting...

author: hoeschec
text:
Went long on USD-CHF.

Good GDP release for the CHF was released this past hour, but the market barely reacted (no follow through) which tells me there may be some strong bulls pushing this pair.

I bought when price RT to the origin of the engulf. Target is shown on chart.

Not sure how this one will turn out, but I want to stay confident in the trade and let it run without micro managing it.

author: hoeschec
text:
USD-CHF update:

On second thought, and after looking closely at the HTF chart

, it appears that price is in no man's land. Although the LTF setup looks good for a long trade, I am going to immediately close out my trade for a positive gain of a couple pips and wait for a better HTF setup.

I really must break this bad habit of only looking at the LTF charts for engulfs and S/R flips. None of that is useful without the bigger picture.

This a bit embarrassing, but oh well

Capital preservation is more important than any one trade.

author: hoeschec
text:
One last post before I fall asleep...

Here are charts for EUR-USD. On the LTF, you can see what appears to be a engulf (almost, but not quite sure). Both flags to the left are important, but it looks like the RBD (Label 2) is only a reaction to the source FL (Label 1). This one is very tempting because there is a clear area for price to RT, and there is a very nice target area with strong R:R. My problem: I don't think the move into the upper flag (labeled 3) is an engulf of Label 2.

So for that reason I will hold off taking this trade.

Any thoughts on my analysis?
